questions.text: Complete the table below, showing the Lewis structure and shape for PF₅ and SeCl₄²⁻.
questions.expectedAnswer: PF₅: Lewis structure shows P central atom with 5 bonding pairs to F atoms, no lone pairs.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: TWO correct Lewis structures with correct shapes. One mark per correct Lewis structure and one mark per correct shape.

questions.text:
The reaction between chlorine trifluoride, ClF₃(g), and hydrazine, N₂H₄(l), is explosive. The reaction is shown below.

4ClF₃(g) + 3N₂H₄(l) → 12HF(g) + 3N₂(g) + 2Cl₂(g)

Calculate ΔᵣH° for the reaction, given the following data.

N₂H₄(l) + O₂(g) → N₂(g) + 2H₂O(l)   ΔᵣH° = −623 kJ mol⁻¹
2ClF₃(g) + 2NH₃(g) → 6HF(g) + N₂(g) + Cl₂(g)   ΔᵣH° = −1200 kJ mol⁻¹
4NH₃(g) + 3O₂(g) → 2N₂(g) + 6H₂O(g)   ΔᵣH° = −1270 kJ mol⁻¹
H₂O(l) → H₂O(g)   ΔᵥₐₚH° = 40.7 kJ mol⁻¹
questions.expectedAnswer: Using Hess's law: Multiply equation 2 by 2: ΔH = −2400 kJ.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Recognises the need to multiply/reverse equations. Merit: Correct process with one error. Excellence: Correct answer with units.

questions.text:
Justify, in terms of the entropy changes of the system and the surroundings, why the reaction between chlorine trifluoride and hydrazine is spontaneous.

4ClF₃(g) + 3N₂H₄(l) → 12HF(g) + 3N₂(g) + 2Cl₂(g)
questions.expectedAnswer: The reaction is highly exothermic (large negative ΔH), so heat is released to the surroundings,...
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Recognises that entropy is positive. Merit: Explains entropy changes for system and surroundings. Excellence: Fully justifies spontaneity linking both contributions.

questions.text:
The table below gives the electron configurations of three elements.

Argon, Ar: 1s²2s²2p⁶3s²3p⁶
Neon, Ne: 1s²2s²2p⁶
Phosphorus, P: 1s²2s²2p⁶3s²3p³

When considering the 3p⁶ part of the electron configuration of argon, what is represented by the following?

3
p
6
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Correctly identifies what each of 3, p, and 6 represents.

questions.text: Arrange the three elements Ar, Ne, and P, in order of decreasing first ionisation energy. Use your knowledge of periodic trends to justify your order.
questions.expectedAnswer: Order: Ne > Ar > P. Ne has the highest IE
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Recognises one factor influencing ionisation energy. Merit: Explains trend with reference to at least two factors (nuclear charge, shielding, distance). Excellence: Justifies the difference for all three elements.

questions.text:
The two possible shapes of bromine trichloride, BrCl₃, are T-shaped and trigonal planar. Both of these shapes are based on the trigonal bipyramidal arrangement of electron pairs around the central atom.

Research shows that the BrCl₃ molecule is polar.

Compare the two possible shapes of the BrCl₃ molecule to identify which shape would result in the BrCl₃ molecule being polar.

Your answer should refer to bond polarity and the arrangement of the bond dipoles.
questions.expectedAnswer: In a trigonal planar shape, the 3 Br–Cl bond dipoles are symmetrically arranged at 120° and...
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Identifies the correct polarity of each shape. Merit: Compares using bond dipole arrangement. Excellence: Fully explains how dipoles cancel/don't cancel for both shapes, including lone pair positions.

questions.text:
Identify all the types of attractive forces between particles of the following substances in their liquid state in the table below.

Ammonia, NH₃ (boiling point −33 °C)
Sulfur dioxide, SO₂ (boiling point −10 °C)
Pentane, CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₃ (boiling point 36 °C)
questions.expectedAnswer: NH₃: Hydrogen bonding, permanent dipole–dipole, temporary dipole (London dispersion forces).
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Two rows correctly identifying the attractive forces for each substance.

questions.text: Explain the difference in the boiling points of ammonia and sulfur dioxide.
questions.expectedAnswer: Despite NH₃ having stronger hydrogen bonding, SO₂ has a higher boiling point (−10 °C vs −33 °C)
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Recognises hydrogen bonding is stronger than permanent/temporary dipole attractions. Merit: Explains why SO₂ has the higher boiling point by linking larger electron cloud to stronger temporary dipole attractions.

questions.text: Explain why the boiling point of pentane is higher than that of sulfur dioxide.
questions.expectedAnswer: Pentane has only temporary dipole forces, but it has a much larger molecular size, greater...
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Recognises molar mass/electron cloud size affects boiling point. Merit: Explains that chain length/surface area gives stronger forces. Excellence: Justifies the difference across ALL three molecules.

questions.text:
The enthalpy of combustion of ethanol, C₂H₅OH, was determined experimentally using the apparatus shown. The ethanol was completely combusted to heat some water in a beaker.

The following data was recorded:
• initial water temperature = 22.1 °C
• final water temperature = 31.2 °C
• initial mass of burner and ethanol = 59.2 g
• final mass of burner and ethanol = 58.7 g

The student calculated the experimental enthalpy change for the combustion of liquid ethanol, ΔcH(C₂H₅OH(l)), to be −770 kJ mol⁻¹.
The specific heat capacity of water is 4.18 J g⁻¹ °C⁻¹.
M(C₂H₅OH) = 46.0 g mol⁻¹

Use the information provided to calculate the mass of the water that was in the beaker.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: One step of calculation correct. Merit: Correct process with one error. Excellence: Correct final mass with units and appropriate significant figures.

questions.text:
Which of these quantities calculated would have been a source of error in the calculated enthalpy value?
Circle your answer.

    temperature change of water          mass of fuel combusted

Explain your choice.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Identifies temperature change of water and states ONE reason. Merit: Identifies temperature change and explains ONE reason for the error.
